sources.title: Waha et al. (2013), Adaptation to climate change through the choice of cropping system and sowing date in sub-Saharan Africa
sources.supports: Joint consideration of crop sequences, sowing date and thermal growing requirements.
sources.does_not_establish: This code is not LPJmL; neither ancient crop calendars nor our second-crop multiplier is validated by that study.

sources.title: Waha et al. (2020), Multiple cropping systems of the world and the potential for increasing cropping intensity
sources.supports: Non-overlapping sequential growing seasons, distinct crop combinations and location-specific limits on intensification.
sources.does_not_establish: Modern observed systems are not 200 AD reconstructions. Second-cycle yields, water, labour and environmental costs cannot be replaced by a universal coefficient.

sources.title: FAO irrigation scheduling, Annex II section 2.1: yield response to evapotranspiration deficit
sources.supports: The relative yield-loss relationship discussed in FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 33.
sources.does_not_establish: The inherited severe-deficit cutoff, irrigation access, ancient absolute yields and reliability factors remain model assumptions. This URL is an annex discussing FAO33, not the full original paper.

sources.title: Allen et al. (1998), Crop evapotranspiration, FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 56
sources.supports: Reference evaporation, crop coefficients and soil-water balance as a process framework.
sources.does_not_establish: Summing water over a candidate season with a reference initial bucket is not a daily coupled crop-sequence water balance or a finite irrigation supply.

sources.title: Sacks et al. (2010), Crop planting dates: an analysis of global patterns
sources.supports: An observed crop-calendar comparison to design before adoption.
sources.does_not_establish: Not yet downloaded or scored in this experiment; modern region-level dates are not ancient observations or pointwise independent ground truth.

comparison_policy.secondary_weight_status: Inherited unvalidated production assumption, preserved solely to isolate calendar-selection effects
comparison_policy.same_crop_status: Inherited restriction; real sequential cropping can repeat a crop, so this is not a general biological prohibition
comparison_policy.water_gate: Unchanged production gate: irrigation share >= 0.5 or growing-period length >= 300 days
comparison_policy.turnaround_status: Resolution sensitivity scenarios, not estimates of ancient farm turnaround time; one bin is about 30.4 days
comparison_policy.perennials: Annual output competes as a sole crop; no invented perennial harvest date or second crop

validation_scope: Exact reproduction of the old single-crop response, calendar-origin invariance, paired comparisons on the previously fixed 4096-cell fantasy sample. These are implementation and diagnostic checks, not independent agronomic validation, estimated population gains or an adoption.
before_production: Validate feasible seasons against observed calendars without tuning on the evaluation locations
Carry a crop-specific soil-water state through the whole sequence, with finite irrigation and growth-stage demand
Use period crop/cultivar, labour and historical yield evidence; review photoperiod and vernalization
Revalidate fallow and historical population-capacity calibration after changing crop mixtures
Evaluate storage across calendar alternatives instead of presenting a tie-broken date as observed
